info.title: Avow's testnet API
info.description:
The API Avow's SDK, verifier and console talk to, on Tempo's Moderato testnet with test dollars. Bodies are JSON, with amounts and times as decimal strings.

Every route but the status routes and a supplier's profile is signed. The request carries an `Authorization` header of the form `Avow signer=<address>, lock=<address>, requestId=<bytes32>, expiry=<unix seconds>, signature=<hex>`. The signature is EIP-712 over an `ApiRequest` naming this API's origin as its audience, the method, the path, the request id, the expiry and the body's hash, under the domain of the business's lock, or of the factory where a route says so. A request stays valid for at most 300 seconds, and a request id is used once. The SDK signs every request, so a caller rarely builds this header by hand, and the API Explorer can send only the unsigned routes.

post.description:
An agent asks a named business for authority, signed by the key it made, under that business's lock. It hears the answer by sending the same request again. The answer carries a pairing code the administrator checks in the console, and once approved, the body the agent enrolls with. The request grants nothing, since only the business account's root key approves.

Avow answers `business.unknown` for an ask signed under any lock it doesn't hold the business at. An account can have a lock at more than one trusted factory, since anyone can create one, so an agent that finds several asks at each until Avow answers.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: Where the request stands: pending, approved or expired

post.summary: Ask for authority without a business
post.description:
An agent asks before it knows its business, signed under the factory. Whoever approves through the link chooses their business, and the approval binds the request to the business whose root key signed the mandate. Once the answer says bound, the agent asks that business as any agent does.

Signed by the agent's key, under the factory's domain.

200.description: Where the request stands: open, bound to a business, or expired

post.description:
An agent enrolls once its key is on the business account, with the mandate the administrator approved. Avow checks the mandate against the account and the transaction that authorized the key.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The agent as Avow enrolled it

post.description:
Avow's relay co-signs a transaction the agent signed with feePayer set, so Avow pays the network fee, or refuses with the cap, rate limit or budget it hit. The relay pays fees only and never moves money into a reserve.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The transaction with the relay as fee payer

post.description:
An agent asks Avow to approve a reserve for terms it agreed with a supplier. Avow checks the mandate, the business's open reserves and any bookings the terms rely on, and answers with a signed approval the lock checks, or a refusal with its reason code. Avow records its decision either way.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: Avow's decision, approved with its signed approval or refused with a reason

post.description:
A supplier asks for a fresh authorization for a commitment's reserve. With it come the approval the reserve was funded under and the buyer's mandate, which the supplier's verifier checks against its own terms and the lock before it accepts.

Signed by the supplier's signing key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: commitmentId
parameters.description: The commitment id, 32 bytes in lower-case hex

200.description: The authorization, approval and mandate, or a refusal with a reason

post.description:
A business cancels after free cancellation has ended, and Avow records when, with its signed timestamp. A late-cancellation charge rests on this record. Before free cancellation ends the business cancels on the lock instead.

Signed by the key of the agent that made the commitment, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: commitmentId
parameters.description: The commitment id, 32 bytes in lower-case hex

200.description: When Avow received the cancellation, and its timestamp

post.description:
A business asks the supplier to start the job, and Avow timestamps the request. The supplier's start receipt names it, and the job can't have started before it.

Signed by the key of the agent that made the commitment, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: commitmentId
parameters.description: The commitment id, 32 bytes in lower-case hex

200.description: The request's digest and Avow's timestamp on it

post.description:
The business's agent passes on the supplier's start receipt for Avow to record.

Signed by the key of the agent that made the commitment, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: commitmentId
parameters.description: The commitment id, 32 bytes in lower-case hex

200.description: Recorded, or refused with a reason

post.description:
The business sends the statement for a contest the lock already took, so Avow holds the text it rules on. Avow records it only when the named transaction holds the lock's Paused event with the statement's reason code and hash.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: commitmentId
parameters.description: The commitment id, 32 bytes in lower-case hex

200.description: The statement's hash and when Avow first recorded it

post.description:
A business registers in the sandbox with a registration its account's root key signed, and Avow pays it test dollars. A sandbox business isn't verified.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The business's id and the test dollars Avow paid it

post.description:
A business registers as a supplier, naming its payee and the signing key that quotes and accepts for it. The account and the signing key both sign the registration.

Signed by the business account's root key, or the signing key it registers, under the factory's domain.

200.description: The supplier's profile as Avow registered it

post.description:
A sandbox business starts a check of itself, and Avow answers with the checker's page, where a person finishes it. A check that's open, in review or passed is answered as it stands, so only a business with no check, or one that was declined or lapsed, starts a new one. The request carries an empty object.

On testnet the checker runs in its own sandbox, so every check is simulated and the answer says so. A check changes no standing of the business and no limit on its agents. For a business that's also a sandbox supplier, a pass lists its account in the testnet's supplier registry, which says a simulated check passed and nothing about a real business.

One request at a time asks the checker about a business. A start that arrives while another asks is refused with `request.in_progress`, and the same request sent again is answered.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The check that started, or the one that already stands

post.description:
Where the business's check stands. While a check is open Avow asks the checker again on each read, so the answer follows the checker's decision. The request carries an empty object.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: Where the business's check stands

post.summary: Top up a sandbox business's test dollars
post.description:
Avow's sandbox faucet sends the business more test dollars, to its own account on Tempo and never to its lock. The request has no body. A business gets one top-up a day, so a second within the day is answered `not_yet` with when to ask again, and sends nothing.

A top-up changes no mandate and no limit. An agent still reserves only what its mandate allows, so any agent the business approved and hasn't revoked can ask for one as well as the root key. Top-ups have a daily total across the sandbox of their own, apart from registrations'. Test dollars have no value.

Signed by the business account's root key, or an agent of the business that isn't revoked, under the business lock's domain.

201.description: The faucet's transfer, or 200 with `not_yet`, and when the business can ask again

post.summary: Ask for a change to authority
post.description:
An agent that holds authority asks for more: a higher limit, a supplier its mandate doesn't name, or open mode on its business's lock. The body also describes an ask for a seller's mandate and an ask to approve one sale, neither of which Avow takes yet. Avow reads what the agent holds now and stores it beside the terms as the request's basis, and answers with the request. The request grants nothing. Only the business account's root key decides it, and an agent can't approve, decline or change one.

The reason is a code from a fixed list, so a request carries no text of the agent's own, apart from the names of what it would sell in an ask for a seller's mandate, and the name, the summary and what counts as delivery of the offer in an ask for one sale. An ask identical to one already waiting is answered with that request. A different ask of the same kind while one waits is refused with `approval_request.already_waiting`, an agent can ask one business for ten changes a day, and after a decline it waits a day before asking the same again. A business decides which kinds its agents may ask for. Avow refuses a kind it doesn't take yet with `approval_request.kind_unavailable`.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

201.description: The request, or 200 with the identical request already waiting

post.description:
Every request the agent made, newest first, up to 200, with where each stands. An agent treats what it asked for as usable only once its request is `active`, since approval and the change landing are separate steps. The request carries an empty object.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The agent's requests

post.description:
Where one of the agent's requests stands. A request of another agent is answered `approval_request.unknown`. The request carries an empty object.

Signed by the agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The request's id, 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The request

post.summary: Read the requests waiting on the administrator
post.description:
The business account's root key reads every request its agents made that is waiting on its administrator, oldest first, so a business's own code or inbox can show them and link each to its signing page. Agent authority requests that named no business aren't in it, since only approving one binds it to a business. The request carries an empty object, and reading changes no request and moves no expiry.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The waiting requests, oldest first

post.description:
The business account's root key approves or declines a request by signing an `ApprovalDecision`, which names the request, the business, the agent, the hash of the exact terms, the hash of the basis and the expiry. The body carries the decision and that signature, and needs no other, since only the root key decides.

Avow checks the signature before it locks anything, then checks the basis again under a lock on the agent or the business. A request whose basis has changed becomes `stale` and never applies, so an approval can't overwrite a newer decision. An approved request is not yet usable. It's `active` once its change has landed, and it lapses if the change hasn't started within an hour. The same decision sent again, even signed afresh, is answered with the request as it stands.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The request's id, 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The request as it stands after the decision

post.summary: Set which changes agents may ask for
post.description:
A business names the changes its agents may ask for. Asking for agent authority is always open, since a request grants nothing. A business that never set a policy lets its agents ask for every change. A request already waiting stays waiting when a kind is taken off.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The policy Avow holds

post.summary: Read which changes agents may ask for
post.description:
The policy the business has, or every change for a business that never set one. The request carries an empty object.

Signed by the business account's root key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The policy Avow holds

get.description: The account, payee and signing key Avow registered for a sandbox supplier. Anyone may read it, unsigned, and a buyer's verifier checks a quote's signature against the signing key.

200.description: The supplier's profile

post.description:
A buyer's agent orders a job from another business, with an expiry. Nothing is reserved until the buyer funds the quote.

Signed by the buyer agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: The order as the mailbox holds it

post.description:
A supplier's agent reads the orders waiting on its business, oldest first.

Signed by the supplier's signing key, under the business lock's domain.

200.description: Up to twenty orders

post.description:
Either side reads one order and where it stands.

Signed by either side's key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id the buyer chose, 16 bytes as 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The order

post.description:
The supplier's agent answers an order with terms it signed.

Signed by the supplier's signing key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id the buyer chose, 16 bytes as 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The order, now quoted

post.description:
The buyer's agent says its reserve is on the lock. Avow reads the lock itself, so the transaction is optional.

Signed by the buyer agent's key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id the buyer chose, 16 bytes as 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The order, now reserved

post.description:
The supplier's agent says the lock shows its acceptance. Avow reads the lock itself, so the transaction is optional.

Signed by the supplier's signing key, under the business lock's domain.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id the buyer chose, 16 bytes as 32 lower-case hex characters

200.description: The order, now accepted
